title: Import and Export Technical Reference
readerIntent: Audit definitions, formats, providers, security, lifecycle, and verification.
owner: Nodics import/export contracts and configured provider modules
summary: A production definition identifies its owner, tenant, source or destination, data contract, limits, processing, policy, run evidence, failure semantics, and provider maturity.

sections.heading: Authority and definitions
items: nImport and nExport orchestrate governed exchange definitions; owning schemas and services validate and persist business data; providers supply trusted source or destination access.
A definition declares format, version, mapping, processors, validators, operation, tenant scope, limits, idempotency, checksum, permissions, audit, and retention.
Input paths and remote locations are resolved through approved aliases and configuration, not unrestricted caller filesystem or URL access.

sections.heading: Import lifecycle
items: Discover and validate input, establish run identity, parse bounded batches, map stable business references, invoke owning models/services, checkpoint, finalize, and record counts and errors.
Core data import is explicit and idempotent; server startup does not repeatedly duplicate persistent sample or application data.
Search indexing, cache invalidation, events, and derived refresh occur after authoritative writes and reconcile independently when partial failure occurs.

sections.heading: Export lifecycle
items: Authorize definition and field projection, read through owning services or approved search contract, paginate deterministically, serialize, checksum, deliver, and record completion.
Exports preserve tenant, masking, classification, purpose, retention, and destination constraints and never expose provider collections as an unrestricted dump.
Incremental export states cursor, revision, deletion, ordering, and replay semantics so retry cannot silently skip or duplicate business records.

sections.heading: Failure, security, and operations
items: Classify malformed, validation, authorization, conflict, duplicate, provider, timeout, and partial failures; resume only from durable verified checkpoints.
Test path traversal, unsupported format, oversized input, malicious fields, cross-tenant references, duplicate run, crash, restart, cleanup, search outage, and rollback.
Monitor run state, throughput, counts, validation categories, checkpoint age, retries, destination delivery, derived lag, and retained artifacts with runbooks.

sections.heading: Definition checklist
items: Stable name, owner, active state, tenant/module scope, permissions, and trigger.
Trusted source or governed destination alias.
Format, version, schema/service/index target, mapping, processors, validators, interceptors, and operation.
Count, size, extension, query, field, batch, timeout, retry, idempotency, and checksum limits.
Diagnostics, run history, audit, reconciliation, rollback, retention, and cleanup.

sections.heading: Test checklist
items: Positive valid and repeat runs.
Negative malformed, unauthorized, cross-tenant, duplicate, oversized, unsupported, and provider-failure cases.
Empty, maximum, batch, streaming, timeout, retry, restart, and partial-failure boundaries.
Schema/search/cache/event/job/workflow/publishing integration.
Live provider, security, performance, recovery, compatibility, and regression.
